refnamediv.refpurpose: An easy to use optical disc burning application with post-burn verification and diagnostic logging

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: xfburn-x is an enhanced fork of Xfce's xfburn based on the libburnia libraries, designed to install cleanly side-by-side with xfburn. It supports burning CD, DVD, and Blu-ray (including M-DISC) media, blanking rewritable discs, creating and burning ISO images, creating audio CDs, automatic post-burn per-sector hash verification, and user-mode diagnostic flight-recorder logging.

refsect1.title: Invocation
refsect1.para: xfburn-x can be called with --burn-image to immediately show the burn image dialog. Optionally the image file can be preselected by appending it to the command line.

When the --data-composition or the --audio-composition option is specified, then xfburn-x's main window will open up with the selected composition type instead of the welcome tab. The filename(s) of the contents of the composition may follow the composition option.

listitem.para: Open the burn image dialog. Optionally the image is given as IMAGE.
Opens xfburn-x with a new data composition. Optionally FILE(S) to be added to the composition follow.
Opens xfburn-x with a new audio composition. Optionally MUSIC FILE(S) to be added to the composition follow.

Selects the transcoder to use when creating audio compositions. Specify list to see all available options. Currently implemented are the gst and the basic transcoder. gst uses gstreamer, and allows the use of any gstreamer-supported media file. basic only allows using audio files already in CD format: uncompressed WAV files.

When the --burn-image or the --blank option is selected, xfburn-x will quit after the dialog exits, unless the --main option is given. In that case the main xfburn-x window is shown after the dialog has been closed.
Write the diagnostic flight-recorder session log to PATH instead of the default directory ~/.local/state/xfburn-x/logs/. Can also be set via the XFBURN_X_LOG_FILE environment variable.
Use the specified X DISPLAY for the user interface.
